Coronary CTA – How to Scan

GE Revolution Vibe (Apex 5.0) · Kenmore only · Step-by-step guide for CT technologists
🚧 DRAFT for review by the cardiac radiologist and lead CT technologist before clinical use. Based on the GE Revolution Vibe Apex 5.0 User Manual (Chapter 13, Cardiac) and GE "Revolution CT Cardiac Overview" (DOC1768328), plus Atrius site rules. Items marked TBD still need a site decision.
Steps
  1. Scheduling & patient prep
  2. Check-in, screening & IV
  3. Position the patient
  4. Attach ECG electrodes
  5. Check the ECG & impedance
  6. Coach the breath-hold
  7. Scouts
  8. Calcium score
  9. Record HR & check Auto Gating

1Scheduling & patient prep

  • Kenmore only – cardiac CTA is performed only on the GE Revolution Vibe at Kenmore.
  • Patient instructions:
    • No caffeine for 12 hours (coffee, tea, energy drinks, chocolate).
    • No exercise / cardiovascular exertion before the exam.
    • No erectile-dysfunction medication (sildenafil, vardenafil, tadalafil) for 4 days.
    • Fast for 4 hours before the exam (GE manual).
  • Heart rate > 80 bpm: request a beta blocker from the ordering provider before scheduling. Target heart rate is low and stable (ideally < 65 bpm).

2Check-in, screening & IV

  • Complete the standard IV-contrast screening and consent per Atrius policy.
  • Check and document heart rate and blood pressure.
  • Explain every part of the exam before you start – a calm, informed patient keeps a steady heart rate.
  • Start the IV outside the scan room to save table time. Explain the warm feeling from the contrast so the patient stays relaxed.
  • Load the injector: contrast + saline (dual barrel). Volume & rate per P3T.
Nitroglycerin: TBD – site protocol pending approval. CT techs do not administer nitroglycerin. Beta blockers per ordering provider / site policy.

3Position the patient

  • Supine, FEET FIRST. Landmark at the sternal notch.
  • Arms above the head, elevated on pillows or sponges. Do not lay the arms flat on the table – it limits vessel flow, causes arm/shoulder motion and makes the patient arch the back as the table moves, causing registration artifacts.
  • Help the patient relax the arms and shoulders (muscle activity shows up on the ECG).
  • Optional: place the grounding wrist strap (skin contact) and connect it to the grounding point behind the integrated cardiac module – improves the ECG signal.
  • Check the gantry display: the selected ECG trigger device (internal ICM) must show connected and active.

4Attach the ECG electrodes

  1. With the arms already up, prep each site: trim hair if needed (shave a 4-inch square on very hairy areas), then scrub with gauze until the skin is pink to remove lotion/oils. Do not use alcohol. GE recommends Nuprep skin-prep gel.
  2. Apply electrodes no more than 5–10 minutes before the scan. Use new GE-recommended, radiolucent, short-term-monitoring electrodes (silver/silver-chloride, fresh gel). Never use dried-out or expired electrodes.
  3. Placement (4 leads):
    • RA and LA: on the middle of the clavicle (move toward the arms for a better signal if needed).
    • RL and LL: at the bottom of the rib cage.
    • Avoid muscle, scar tissue and hair. Keep electrodes as far as possible from the scan field.
  4. Route all four lead cords together on ONE side of the patient, using the lead-bridge clips. Secure the cables so they do not dangle from the table – cable movement during the scan degrades the signal.

5Check the ECG & electrode impedance

  • Review the ECG waveform. Heart rate must be within system limits (30–200 bpm); a low, stable heart rate gives the best images at the lowest dose.
  • Always run the impedance check: right-click the ECG waveform → Test Electrode Impedance (or the Check Impedance icon on the gantry display). Green = good, Red = poor – reposition and re-test any red electrode until all pass.
  • If the patient moves, re-check impedance.
Do not scan until you have an acceptable waveform and heart rate. Avoid "Override" on a low-signal alert – it can cause erratic triggering or a scan abort.

6Coach the breath-hold

  • Give the same breathing instructions for every series, starting with the scout (Auto Voice keeps them consistent). Instructions should be 10 seconds or longer so the patient breathes slowly.
  • After "take a breath in and hold it", leave 3–5 seconds of silence – the heart rate takes 2–7 seconds to settle after the breath-hold. Watch the ECG to see when it stabilizes. (Auto Voice Preset Delay can add 1–7 s before X-ray on.)
  • Practice the breath-hold with the patient before scanning.
  • If the patient struggles to hold their breath, 2–4 L oxygen by nasal cannula per physician/site policy can help and may lower the heart rate.

7Scouts

  1. Select the patient, connect the IV to the contrast tubing, review breathing instructions.
  2. Select the Coronary CTA protocol → Accept → review settings → Confirm Settings → Move to Scan.
  3. Give the breathing instructions → Start Scan. Acquire both scouts (AP and lateral).
  4. If the scout shows the patient off-center by more than 2 cm, the system shows the table height to use – adjust with the gantry elevation controls.

8Calcium score (non-contrast)

  • Gated, non-contrast acquisition covering the whole heart. GE recommended settings: GE CACS Auto Gating profile, 120 kV, 0.28 s rotation, 2.5 mm, 160 mm coverage, DFOV 25 cm, Noise Index 20, ASiR-V 50%.
  • Adjust the Graphic Rx to fully cover the heart. Same breathing instructions as practiced.
  • The heart rate is recorded automatically during this breath-hold if the scan is at least as long as the breath-hold recording length.
  • Use these images to set the start/end of the CCTA and the SmartPrep monitoring level.

9Record the heart rate & check Auto Gating

  • Auto Gating uses the heart rate and variability from the most recent breath-hold recording to set the acquisition window (marked with a white dot).
  • If the heart rate has changed, or you need a fresh recording: in the Acquisition Window & Heart Rate widget click Record New HR (practice breath-hold).
  • Check ECG & Gating: Auto Gating = On, profile GE CCTA (Nominal). Use Extra Large Pt CCTA for very large patients.
  • Auto Gating picks the phases by heart rate: low HR → mid-diastole (~75%); intermediate HR (70s–mid 80s) → mid-diastole + end-systole; high HR → end-systole (~40–55%).
  • Irregular rhythm: keep Smart Arrhythmia Management On (automatic rescan of a bad beat) and consider a larger HR Variation Allowance.

10Set up the CCTA & SmartPrep

  • Confirm the ECG trace is strong and stable and a cardiac scan mode (Cardiac Axial) is selected.
  • Select the Cardiac SFOV (Small / Medium / Large by patient size).
  • Coverage: from about 1 cm above the left main coronary ostium to 1 cm below the cardiac apex. With 160 mm coverage the heart is usually one exposure.
  • SmartPrep: place the monitoring ROI on the descending aorta. GE typical cardiac SmartPrep settings: monitoring delay 10 s, inter-scan delay 1.7 s (an image every 2 s), enhancement threshold 150 HU, diagnostic delay = Auto Minimum.
  • Enter the contrast in the Contrast collection. Volume & rate per P3T, with a saline chaser – the end of the contrast injection to X-ray on should not exceed about 6 seconds.
  • Arm the injector → Confirm Settings.
A leftover SmartPrep group can carry into a protocol unused – delete it if it is not needed. "Acquire Baseline" stays grey until all SmartPrep baseline images finish reconstructing.

11Inject & scan

  1. Give the same breathing instructions as the previous series.
  2. Move to Scan → Start Scan. With the integrated injector, the injection starts automatically when you press Start Scan.
  3. Watch the SmartPrep monitoring images; the scan triggers when the ROI reaches threshold.
  4. If the R-peak signal is lost after Start Scan, the system continues with simulated R-peaks at the last heart rate and shows an alert – pause/abort if you do not want to continue.

12Recon checks & send

  • Secondary recons: confirm Auto Gating = Link (not Unlink) so phase and SnapShot Freeze are set by the profile. If a recon shows Unlink, check the SnapShot Freeze field yourself.
  • Coronary recon: 0.625 mm; SmartPhase or phase per Auto Gating; SnapShot Freeze On. Recommended manual multi-phase: 70–80% in 5% steps. DFOV ≥ 15 cm with at least 2 cm of tissue around the heart (do not over-zoom).
  • The ECG trace is saved automatically as Series 599 (record only – not diagnostic).
  • Send per the cardiac reference book: the calcium score series to the GE AW Server for the SmartScore report (step 13); the cardiac CTA to TeraRecon; reformats to Synapse.
🚧 In the works: step-by-step coronary CTA post-processing in TeraRecon (workflow, reformats, what is sent to Synapse) is being written by the site, with screenshots.
Series & Reconstructions for the Vibe: TBD. The old "40 mm / 0.35 s / SnapShot Segment" settings in the protocol guide are from the previous scanner and do not apply to the Vibe. Confirm the Vibe recon chain at the console.

13Calcium score report on GE AW Server (SmartScore)

🚧 In the works: the step-by-step SmartScore process (with screenshots) is being written by the site. Until then, follow the confirmed points below.
  • Send the gated, non-contrast calcium score series to the GE AW Server and open it in SmartScore. Never score the contrast CTA series.
  • Scoring is automatic with the GE settings (including artery labeling) – do not change the GE scoring settings.
  • Select the patient's ethnicity in SmartScore (from Epic – confirm with the patient if missing) so the report shows the MESA percentile. If the percentile shows n/a, the ethnicity was not selected.
  • Save the report and send it to Synapse. A score of 0 still gets a report.

14After the scan

  • Remove electrodes, check the IV site and monitor the patient per contrast policy.
  • If any medication was given per site protocol, recheck vitals and document in Epic.

15Troubleshooting

ProblemWhat to do
Low Signal alert / noisy waveformCheck cable connections; run the impedance check; re-prep (gauze/Nuprep, no alcohol) and apply fresh electrodes; try another active lead (I, II, III or Auto). The alert blocks Confirm Settings until resolved or overridden – avoid Override.
Double trigger on a tall T-waveChange the active lead and/or electrode position; re-check impedance.
"ICM disconnected" on the gantry when it is connectedClear it from the gantry Cardiac settings menu by changing a setting such as Active Lead.
Irregular beats / arrhythmiaSmart Arrhythmia Management On; after the scan use the ECG Editor (insert/delete/move R-peaks) or Switch Scan to reconstruct from the second exposure.
Heart rate high or risingRe-coach and repeat the practice breath-hold; record a new HR; Auto Gating shifts to end-systole automatically. Consult the radiologist about beta blockers per site policy.
Blur across the whole imageUsually breathing/patient motion, not cardiac – re-coach the breath-hold.
Noisy images in a large patientCheck projected vs target Noise Index before scanning; consider the Extra Large Pt CCTA profile.

Sources: MESA CAC Score Reference Values (mesa-nhlbi.org/node/51); GE Revolution Vibe Apex 5.0 User Manual (UM 6789320-1EN), Chapter 13 Cardiac – figures reproduced for internal Atrius training; GE "Revolution CT Cardiac Overview" (DOC1768328); Atrius CT Protocol Guide site rules (Kenmore only, P3T contrast, SmartPrep ROI on the descending aorta). For technologist reference only – follow the console and site protocol.
